title: Delhi's Beloved All American Diner Returns After Five Years, Now in Hyderabad
excerpt: The India Habitat Centre institution, closed since 2021, returns at The Loft in HITEC City with checkerboard floors, a jukebox, and a meal for two at about ₹1,500.
body:
• The All American Diner opens to the public in Hyderabad on 23 September 2026 at Ground Floor, The Loft, Silpa Gram Craft Village, HITEC City — the first outlet in the brand's new expansion.
  • It is the same brand that ran at Delhi's India Habitat Centre from 2001 to 2021 under Rohit Khattar's Old World Hospitality, now revived under his EHV International.
  • Standouts from the preview menu: Rodeo Lamb Burger, Nashville Fried Chicken Burger, barbecue wings, crazy shakes and a playful cocktail list including a Popcorn Manhattan.
  • What this means for you: if you are in Hyderabad for the festival season, budget about ₹1,500 plus taxes for two (food only) — and Delhi expats finally get their Habitat ritual back.

A Delhi institution finds a second home

Five years after Delhi's beloved All American Diner shut its doors at India Habitat Centre, the name is back — in Hyderabad. The diner opens to the public on 23 September 2026 at The Loft in HITEC City, the same complex that already houses Rohit Khattar's Fireback, Barback and Hosa.

The original opened at India Habitat Centre in 2001 under Khattar's Old World Hospitality and spent two decades becoming part of the capital's cultural furniture. It closed in 2021 when the group's Habitat contract ended and the space became Habitat Hub. The Hyderabad outlet, now under Khattar's EHV International, is the first restaurant in the brand's new expansion.

The 18 September preview: checkerboard floors, cherry-red vinyl booths, chrome everywhere, vintage American tin plaques on the walls — Route 66, Babe Ruth, Mobilgas, a New York taxi rate card — and a limited-edition Elvis Wurlitzer jukebox by the pastry counter.

Context & Background

The diner was one of India's earliest proper American diner experiences: red booths, pop-culture memorabilia, all-day breakfast energy, hot dogs, burgers, pancakes, malts and shakes. For Delhi regulars it was never only about the food — the ritual was a play at the Habitat, earnest talk about art, then the undoing of all that sophistication over fries and a thick shake.

Twenty years is a long time in restaurant years, and the 2021 closure landed like a small bereavement among loyalists. Khattar's Hyderabad run has been swift: Thai cooking at Fireback led by David Thompson's team, the cocktail-led Barback inspired by Bangkok's Chinatown, regional South Indian cooking at Hosa — and now the diner. His restaurant family also includes Indian Accent, Comorin and Chor Bizarre.

Impact & Analysis

The revival reflects a wider shift: brands with genuine emotional equity are being brought back rather than invented from scratch. Hyderabad — which Khattar's team calls one of India's most exciting culinary destinations — was chosen as the first stop in EHV International's South India push.

The early evidence is encouraging. The Rodeo Lamb Burger (grilled quarter-pound lamb patty with cheddar, red onions, pickles and iceberg) and the Nashville Fried Chicken Burger (buttermilk fried chicken tossed in Nashville hot sauce with jalapeño relish) drew real praise at the preview, along with stuffed barbecue wings. The table card warned of a much larger full menu to come — "give us time to dress up" — so the preview is only a taste.

"Hyderabad has emerged as one of India's most exciting culinary destinations, with an audience that deeply appreciates quality, innovation and hospitality."

— Rohit Khattar, Founder Chairman, EHV International

Beyond the burgers: a Chili Dog, Bacon Jam Benedict, pancakes with butter and maple syrup, a strawberry cream crazy shake, the classic banana split. Vegetarians are covered too: a spiced black-bean Veggie Burger, Mushroom & Cheese Florentine, Sweet Corn & Jalapeño Chowder and an adaptable Caesar salad. Behind the bar, head of bars Varun Sharma has built a playful list — a Creamsicle Highball, a Popcorn Manhattan on toasted popcorn vermouth, a Lunch Box Punch with peanut butter wash, and frozen margaritas, daiquiris and piña coladas. Executive chef Sumit Sawardekar leads the kitchen. Even the menu cover keeps the old cheek: "Come Hungry, Leave Grinnin'."

Diaspora Angle

For US-based readers, this is the India-homecoming version of the classic diner craving: returnees who queued for burgers and bottomless coffee in American college towns can now get the real article without the transatlantic flight. Visiting Hyderabad this festival season? Find it at Ground Floor, The Loft, Silpa Gram Craft Village, HITEC City — roughly ₹1,500 plus taxes for two, food only; cocktails and crazy shakes cost extra.

What's Next

The immediate question is how the full menu lands once the kitchen settles in — and how closely Hyderabad's room recreates the Delhi ritual once the novelty fades. The larger one is whether this is a one-city homecoming or the start of a genuine multi-city revival. As the first-look review concluded: go for the nostalgia, stay for the burgers and wings.
